Let the matrix be $A$.
$A = \left(\n\begin{array}{cccc}\n \frac{4}{3} & 1 & -\frac{9}{2} & -\frac{13}{3} \\\n -\frac{13}{3} & \frac{25}{6} & -\frac{19}{6} & \frac{11}{6} \\\n -\frac{23}{6} & \frac{29}{6} & -\frac{10}{3} & -\frac{19}{6} \\\n -\frac{17}{6} & -\frac{7}{6} & \frac{5}{2} & \frac{7}{3} \\\n\end{array}\n\right)$

To get rid of fractions, we can multiply the whole matrix by 6:
$6A = \left(\n\begin{array}{cccc}\n 8 & 6 & -27 & -26 \\\n -26 & 25 & -19 & 11 \\\n -23 & 29 & -20 & -19 \\\n -17 & -7 & 15 & 14 \\\n\end{array}\n\right)$
Then $\det(6A) = 6^4 \det(A)$.

The determinant of the original matrix is
$\det(A) = \frac{\det(6A)}{6^4} = \frac{\det(6A)}{1296}$

Calculate the determinant of 6A using a computer or calculator.
$\det(6A) = \left| \n\begin{array}{cccc}\n 8 & 6 & -27 & -26 \\\n -26 & 25 & -19 & 11 \\\n -23 & 29 & -20 & -19 \\\n -17 & -7 & 15 & 14 \\\n\end{array}\n\right| = 0$

Thus $\det(A) = \frac{0}{1296} = 0$.
Final Answer: The final answer is $\boxed{0}$
